transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Li (Product), Ellen Park (NovaChain CTO), Rajesh Iyer (Lead ML), Maya Lopez (SRE), Tom Bennett (PM)

--- Optional Summary / Topics (auto) ---
Summary: demo covering long-context behavior, throughput limits, and streaming/backpressure/timeouts. Showed Console, API examples, and Optimize recommendations.
Topics: long context tokens, KV cache, batching, streaming backpressure, timeout handling, dedicated clusters, quantization tradeoffs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll jump in with a short agenda. Marco will demo the API and Console then we'll run through Optimize suggestions and finish with a Q&A.
[00:12] Ellen: awesome, thanks. we mostly want to validate long-doc summarization and also understand how you handle sustained spikes, like 5-10k requests per second.
[00:20] Sofia: yup that aligns. quick intro from our side, Marco is our systems SE who runs the perf runs, Dana on product who will show the Console.
[00:30] Marco: hi all. quick note, i'm going to intentionally push some backpressure scenarios in the demo, so you'll see streaming stalls and timeouts on purpose so we can talk through mitigation.
[00:42] Rajesh: perfect, that's exactly what we need. first question though - our documents can be up to 1M tokens in some flows, how does Redwood handle very long context?
[00:55] Marco: great question. so we have two paths depending on deployment - for Hosted API we do prefix eviction and smart KV cache heuristics, for Dedicated/Private we give you more control: configurable KV cache sizing, segmented context windows and chunked attention optimizations. in practice we chunk large docs and maintain a compressed kv cache.
[01:15] Maya: is that something we configure in Console or in the API call? like v2 payload options?
[01:22] Marco: both - the Console has a profile you can tweak (we'll show it) and the API supports context-hint headers to say whether to stream/attach or to use chunking. note: transcription -- sometimes the header names show up slightly different in older SDKs.
[01:35] Tom: and the difference in latency if you chunk vs full-attend?
[01:39] Marco: chunked approach trades a few tens of ms on average per request for huge memory savings; for 1M token jobs it's the only way to avoid OOMs unless you offload. we also show quantized variants that cut memory by ~2-4x but with a small quality hit.
[01:55] Sofia: ok dana can you pull up the Console and show the KV/cache and Optimize tab?
[02:02] Dana: sure. switching windows... bear with me, screen might be a bit laggy. (brief pause) alright, Console > Models > Profiles. here is the 'long-context' profile we pre-configured for NovaChain - you'll see cache size, max prefix retention and preferred quantization setting.
[02:20] Ellen: looks good. can you connect that to a live API request?
[02:24] Marco: yes i'll fire a demo script that simulates 2k tps for 30s then ramp to 10k for 60s, with a mix of long (200k tokens) and short requests. you'll see streaming backpressure on the client.
[02:38] [sfx: keyboard typing]
[02:45] Marco: kicking off run... starting baseline 2k tps now.
[02:52] [00:30 into demo / automated run logs suppressed in transcript]
[03:22] Rajesh: i'm seeing steady latency at ~120ms p50, p95 spikes to 450ms during batching windows - is that expected?
[03:31] Marco: yes, we put in a continuous batching algorithm; p95 spikes correspond to batching boundary alignment and KV fetches. those are tunable by the batching window and also by route-level priority.
[03:42] Maya: ok at what point do you start dropping requests or throttle? we need hard SLOs.
[03:48] Marco: in Hosted mode we have a soft throttle and reject strategy when queues exceed capacity; in Dedicated you can define queue depth and autoscale/burst behaviors - we also recommend a fallback model tier for graceful degradation.
[04:00] Ellen: and for streaming backpressure? our clients rely on streaming chunks and we don't want timeouts to invalidate sessions.
[04:07] Marco: streaming backpressure happens when downstream clients can't keep up; our runtime supports windowed streaming with resume tokens so you can reconnect and continue the stream - if the client times out we persist the KV to allow resumed generation. note: resume tokens are in beta for some model families.
[04:25] Tom: will that work with web-socket vs server-sent events?
[04:29] Marco: yes both. SSE and websockets supported, we surface the same resume token semantics. implementation detail: some older SDKs mishandle partial frames, so we recommend the latest JS and Python SDKs.
[04:40] [demo ramping to 10k tps - more logs suppressed]
[05:10] Rajesh: ok we've hit a bunch of dropped streams, seeing intermittent timeouts around 8s. what timeout do you recommend for clients?
[05:18] Marco: client timeout should be tuned to expected tail latency; for our long-context heavy requests we suggest 15-20s to account for batching and KV fetches, or better: use streaming with resume tokens and a short window heartbeat so you don't close the TCP connection.
[05:33] Maya: what about retries? we need idempotency guarantees for certain endpoints.
[05:38] Marco: we recommend idempotency keys for generation endpoints; for stateful sessions (long context KV) we pair keys with session ids so retries resume rather than duplicate. there is a small risk of duplicate token emission but we have a dedupe window in the server.
[05:55] Ellen: security question - if we use Private deployment with VPC and on-prem, is KMS/HSM supported and do you integrate with our audit logs?
[06:03] Sofia: yes. Private includes KMS integrations (AWS/GCP/Azure) and HSM option for key custody, plus audit log forwarders and SIEM connectors. we'll attach the SOC2+ISO packet after the call.
[06:14] Rajesh: great. can you also share perf counters and raw streaming logs from the demo so we can run our analysis?
[06:21] Marco: will do - i'll upload the raw logs to the shared benchmark sheet and mark the rows with the test id.
[06:27] [Demo run completes; recap screen shown]
[06:40] Tom: quick question on cost - at 10k sustained tps what's the expected $/1M tokens? rough order of magnitude?
[06:48] Sofia: cost depends on model variant, quantization, and batching effectiveness. rough ballpark for optimized quantized model on Dedicated is 30-50% of naive hosted cost; we'll send an estimated cost model for your traffic profile.
[07:00] Rajesh: are there any gotchas with autoscaling and GPU warmup that can cause requests to time out during a scale event?
[07:07] Marco: warmup can add a couple of hundred ms per instance; to avoid user-impact we recommend overprovisioned buffer plus burst capacity, and we have fast pool spin-up for common instance types (we pre-warm kernels). also set route-level fallback to a smaller model until warmup completes.
[07:23] Maya: earlier you mentioned quantization causing small quality regressions - how do you validate regressions?
[07:29] Dana: we tie quality monitoring to evals in Optimize; you can upload prompt sets, we run A/B with golden metrics and raise regression alerts. for critical paths we recommend periodic full-precision checks.
[07:43] Ellen: ok let's talk pilot - we want a 2-week pilot with 1 dedicated pool, production-grade monitoring, and a small SL (maybe 20% traffic) to start. can you support that timeline?
[07:52] Sofia: yes we can. next steps: we'll send pricing for Dedicated + pilot, Marco will run a full 10k TPS benchmark on our infra by 2027-01-04, and we'll provision Console access.
[08:02] Rajesh: one more technical nit - you said resume tokens are beta, what model families support them?
[08:08] Marco: currently GPT-style attention families and several open Llama-derivatives; models with chunked attention support it better. we'll include exact family list in the benchmark sheet notes.
[08:20] [cross talk, some participants typing]
[08:30] Maya: a question about observability - can we get token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns in Console?
[08:36] Dana: yep, Console has token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and trace hooks; you can export to Prometheus or forward to DataDog.
[08:45] Tom: do you have a canned playbook for on-call SREs for timeouts/backpressure events?
[08:49] Marco: yes we give runbooks: increase queue depth, enable fallback model, check KV cache hit rates, force immediate autoscale. we'll share the doc in the shared folder.
[08:58] Ellen: any blockers from our side for pilot? we have to sign a DPA and we need SSO (SAML).
[09:05] Sofia: we support SAML SSO and will send DPA + SOC2 within 24 hours.
[09:12] Rajesh: ok great. last practical question: does the SDK expose metrics for streaming backpressure (e.g., client lag, resume token usage)?
[09:20] Marco: yes metrics emitted to your telemetry include stream_lag_ms, resume_tokens_emitted, kv_cache_hits, batching_window_ms. SDKs also export hooks for custom telemetry.
[09:28] Ellen: nice. thanks everyone, good session.
[09:32] Sofia: recap of next steps: we'll email pricing and docs, Marco uploads benchmark logs & schedule pilot kickoff for Jan 5, Dana will create Console demo access.
[09:40] Tom: thanks, talk soon.
[09:42] [call end]
